statements.justification: Values match: Ccl6 Arctic_vs_WT +1.32/+1.19/+0.90 from 5mo; ArcticC5aR1KO_vs_Arctic +0.08 to +0.42, so no reversal. Useful nuance: not every Arctic-induced chemokine depends on C5aR1. Cited [1] lists other chemokines, not Ccl6. Ccl6 is reported in plaque-associated microglia of other AD models.

All values match (Arctic_vs_WT +0.21 to +1.20; ArcticC5aR1KO_vs_Arctic -0.96 to -0.66 at every age; C5aR1KO_vs_WT 2mo -0.95). The paper puts Cxcl2 in cluster 4 and validates it by RT-PCR: up in Arctic at 5mo, lower in Arctic/C5aR1KO. Both citations support the context.
statements.in_paper_where: Results, 'Pathway analysis reveals less inflammation...'; Fig. 5a and 5c (RT-PCR)

statements.justification: Values match (Arctic_vs_WT +0.28/+0.57 at 7/10mo; ArcticC5aR1KO_vs_Arctic -1.43 to -0.83; C5aR1KO_vs_WT 2mo -2.06). The paper also finds Vegfa lower in Arctic/C5aR1KO (RT-PCR -46% at 5mo). 'Angiogenic factor' is textbook, not the paper's point; the cited human VEGF review is only loosely relevant.
statements.in_paper_where: Results, Fig. 5a and 5c (Vegfa in cluster 4; RT-PCR -46% in Arctic/C5aR1KO at 5mo)

statements.justification: Values match (Arctic -1.06 at 2mo, +2.06/+1.96 at 5/7mo; KO -0.14/-0.16). Axl as a plaque-microglia gene fits [5]. 'Normalises' is loose: Arctic/KO at 2mo ends about +0.7 above WT (-1.06+1.77), so KO overshoots the dip. Axl is not in the paper; n=2 per group.

Numbers match (Hck -0.36 at 10mo; KO +0.29 at 2mo) and the statement itself calls them mild. The Aβ-clearance link is hedged and plausible, but a 0.3 log2 shift with two mice per group is near noise, and [6] concerns Hck knockout in J20 mice, not a small mRNA change.

Quoted values are right, but 'C5aR1-dependent' is overstated: suppression shows at 2 and 7mo only. At 10mo it is +0.13 (Arctic) and +0.12 (WT); WT 5mo is -0.06. The GM-CSF work in rat microglia [7] says nothing about C5aR1, or that losing Stat5a would blunt responses.

'Restored' is read from the wrong contrast: C5aR1KO_vs_WT is the KO effect without the transgene. The contrast that tests restoration, ArcticC5aR1KO_vs_Arctic, is +0.19, -0.13, +0.09, +0.09, so the Arctic decline (-0.31 at 7mo) is not restored. The Arctic decline itself is right but small.

Values match (Tlr2 +0.44/+0.62 at 5/7mo; Cd14 +0.38 at 2mo to +1.02 at 5mo). CD14/TLR2/TLR4 as the fAβ receptor complex driving signalling and phagocytosis is correctly cited [8,9]. The paper lists Tlr2 as a phagocytosis receptor but never mentions Cd14; Cd14 already rises at 2mo, so 'mid-late' fits Tlr2 better.
statements.in_paper_where: Results (Fig. 6a, Tlr2 among phagocytosis-promoting receptors in cluster 2) and Discussion (fibrillar Aβ is a TLR2/TLR4 ligand); Cd14 not mentioned

overall.comment: The interpretation gets the strongest, best-known part right: Cxcl2 and Vegfa are up in Arctic and lower without C5aR1, as the paper reports, and Ccl6, Axl, Tlr2 and Cd14 are sensible plaque-microglia additions the paper did not discuss. It slips on the weakest genes: Cx3cr1 'restoration' reads the wrong contrast (C5aR1KO_vs_WT) and Stat5a 'C5aR1-dependence' rests on two of four ages, with Hck at noise level. It reaches the paper's inflammatory-gene conclusion but not the phagosome/lysosome one, and its walk-leg database edges add nothing.
